name: Auditory Attention
definition: The ability to focus on a single source of sound in the presence of other distracting sounds.

benchmark.name: WSJ0-2mix
benchmark.metric: SI-SNRi (scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio improvement), dB; higher is better
benchmark.human_reference: General working adults with normal hearing who must follow one talker among competing talkers (e.g., open offices, meetings, customer-facing roles).

benchmark.name: WHAM!
benchmark.metric: dB SI-SNRi (scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio improvement), WHAM! test set, 8 kHz min mode
benchmark.human_reference: General adult listeners with normal hearing. Auditory attention is a general ability used in everyday work settings such as offices, phone calls, meetings and noisy workplaces.

benchmark.name: WSJ0-2mix
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, the people who use auditory attention at work to follow one talker among others (meetings, call centers, noisy workplaces).

benchmark.name: WSJ0-2mix
benchmark.metric: SI-SDRi (dB, scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio improvement; higher is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult working population with normal hearing (people who routinely must follow one talker among competing voices, e.g., in offices, meetings, customer-facing and control-room settings)

benchmark.name: WHAMR!
benchmark.metric: SI-SNRi (scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio improvement), dB, higher is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal hearing: people who routinely follow one talker in noisy, reverberant settings such as cafes, restaurants and open offices.

benchmark.name: WHAMR!
benchmark.metric: SI-SNRi, dB (higher is better); SDRi 18.2 dB
benchmark.human_reference: General adult listeners with normal hearing: the typical person who must follow one talker amid competing speech, noise and room reverberation at work. Examples are open offices, meetings and call centres. They listen monaurally, as on a single-channel recording or phone line.

benchmark.name: Libri2Mix
benchmark.human_reference: General adult listeners with normal hearing, the typical people who must follow one talker amid a competing talker at work. The comparison is to a median listener attending to one voice in a single-channel two-talker mixture at roughly equal level.
